purpose: MFPI after verified-pilot-3.12: a peer-reviewed analysis of the species itself as its own nutrition row when neither RDA DB 10.4 nor MEXT 2020 has a row for it (team-lead decision 2026-10-01, route 3, factor 0.85). Read only by configs that name this file.
rule: Used only when no RDA row is linked to the species and no MEXT species row exists. The paper must identify the species (morphology or molecular), analyse raw edible tissue, and report the moisture of the same sample. Dry-basis values are converted to fresh weight as value_dw x (100 - moisture) / 100; mg/kg dry weight is first divided by 10 to give mg per 100 g dry weight. A component the paper reports inconsistently is left out (3.7 minimum-components rule), never guessed. The row is ranked against the fixed cohort of its RDA group plus itself and never joins a cohort.

items.part: whole soft body (flesh), 25 oysters pooled per replicate, 4 replicates
items.sample: Cultured oysters, 20 months old, commercial size, sampled in February before gametogenesis; Xiangshan Bay, Ningbo, Zhejiang, China (29.47 N, 121.42 E); 100 individuals; species confirmed by species-specific molecular markers on the adductor muscle
items.region: Xiangshan Bay, Ningbo, Zhejiang, China (29.47 N, 121.42 E)
items.sample_period: February, before gametogenesis (year not stated; paper published July 2021)
items.taxon_link_evidence: The paper identifies every sampled oyster by species-specific molecular methods and names it Crassostrea sikamea, which WoRMS resolves to Magallana sikamea (836041).
items.moisture_method: Each oyster: (soft weight - freeze-dried soft weight) / soft weight; Table 1 mean 84.9 ± 3.3%

protein_g.reported: Protein 39.5 ± 2.3% of dry weight (Kjeldahl, N x 6.25)

omitted.zinc_mg: Table 1 gives Zn 1,164 ± 30 and Cu 493 ± 11 mg/kg dry weight for C. sikamea, but the Results text says 'Cu and Zn were also significantly higher in Kumamoto oysters (1,164 and 493 mg/kg)', the reverse order. The zinc value is ambiguous inside the paper and is left out of the mean (not 0).

edible_fraction.method: mean soft weight 3.0 ± 0.7 g / mean total weight 14.6 ± 3.2 g (Table 1, oysters in shell)
edible_fraction.limitations: Ratio of means of 100 cultured oysters of 20 months; shell share varies with size, season and culture site.

items.limitations: One bay, one season (February) and one age class; dry-basis values converted with the mean moisture of the same oysters, so the fresh-weight values carry the moisture spread (± 3.3%). Different laboratory, method and region from the RDA cohort foods. Ranked against the RDA marine-animal cohort plus itself; never a cohort member.

items.part: edible portion = the upper two thirds of the plant length; the lower rigid portion was discarded (Section 2.2)
items.sample: Wild Sargassum horneri harvested from the Chikuzen Sea, Fukuoka, Japan, once or twice a month; the six dates with both proximate and mineral data (19 Jan, 14 Feb, 28 Feb, 28 Mar, 21 Apr and 11 May 2005) are averaged. One pooled sample of 7-20 plants per date, each measured 2-4 times; from 28 February the male and female plants were analysed apart and the paper's own (Average) row is used.
items.sample_period: 19 January to 11 May 2005 (six harvest dates); collected once or twice a month from November 2004
items.taxon_link_evidence: The paper analyses Sargassum horneri (Turner) C. Agardh, which is the WoRMS accepted name of 괭생이모자반 (494853); no other species is in the samples.
items.moisture_method: Table 3, mean of the six dates: water lost by lyophilization plus the weight lost by drying the pulverized sample at 105 C for 5 h, measured on the same pooled sample as the components (Section 2.3.1), 893/894/879/860/866/888 mg/g.

protein_g.reported: Table 3, protein on a dry weight basis: 88.0 / 128 / 105 / 63.5 / 63.7 / 70.4 mg/g (Kjeldahl N x 6.25, AOAC 1995); mean 86.43 mg/g = 8.643 g per 100 g dry weight.

calcium_mg.reported: Table 4, calcium on a dry weight basis: 13.3 / 12.5 / 11.9 / 10.7 / 11.8 / 13.7 mg/g (AOAC 1995); mean 12.317 mg/g = 1,231.7 mg per 100 g dry weight.

zinc_mg.reported: Table 4, zinc on a dry weight basis: 46.5 / 41.4 / 41.0 / 38.4 / 38.6 / 34.5 ug/g (AOAC 1995); mean 40.07 ug/g = 4.007 mg per 100 g dry weight.

omitted.iron_mg: The paper does not analyse iron: Table 4 reports calcium, magnesium and zinc only, and iron appears nowhere in the text. It is left out of the mean (not 0) under the 3.7 minimum-components rule.

edible_fraction.method: The paper's own definition of the edible portion: the upper two thirds of the plant length, with the lower rigid portion discarded (Section 2.2). Taken as 2/3.
edible_fraction.limitations: This is the paper's length ratio, not a measured weight ratio, and the lower portion is the thicker part, so the true edible share by weight is probably lower than 2/3. The paper reports no refuse percentage.

items.limitations: One bay in Japan (Chikuzen Sea, Fukuoka), one season (January to May 2005), and one pooled sample per date, so the value carries no Korean sampling. Protein is Kjeldahl nitrogen x 6.25, which overstates protein in seaweed because of non-protein nitrogen; the paper itself reports a lower pure-protein figure for other species. Iron is not measured, so the mean rests on three of the four components. Cross-checks against the paper's own text: the January protein converts to 9.42 mg/g against the 9.4 mg/g the paper prints, and the six-date means (1.04 g protein, 88.0% moisture per 100 g) match the abstract's seasonal means of 1.0% protein and 87.7% moisture.
